prompt: Which row correctly classifies the four physical quantities?
options: distance: scalar; displacement: vector; speed: scalar; velocity: vector
distance: vector; displacement: scalar; speed: vector; velocity: scalar
distance: scalar; displacement: scalar; speed: vector; velocity: vector
distance: vector; displacement: vector; speed: scalar; velocity: scalar

answer.explanation: Distance and speed have magnitude only and are scalars. Displacement and velocity have magnitude and direction and are vectors.

distractor_explanations: Incorrect. Reverses the classifications for all four quantities.
Incorrect. Displacement is a vector, not a scalar.
Incorrect. Distance is a scalar, not a vector.
hints: Ask whether each quantity requires a direction to be completely specified.
Distance is how far without direction; displacement is change of position in a specified direction.
solution: Distance (scalar), displacement (vector), speed (scalar), velocity (vector). Option 1 is correct.
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: Test distance: 10 m has no direction, so distance is scalar.
Step 2: Test displacement: 10 m north has direction, so displacement is vector.
Step 3: Test speed: rate of change of distance (magnitude only), so speed is scalar.
Step 4: Test velocity: rate of change of displacement (has direction), so velocity is vector.
lesson_anchors: A common mistake: the unit or the story does not decide
exclusions: vector addition and resolution deferred to l11
